Subject: RE: Discovery — Redwood integration / observability items (post-call recap)

Thanks again for taking the time today — really useful call. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Call recap:
- Goals: integrate Redwood for chat + reranker for search results; surface embeddings for re-ranking and personalization; keep latency under 200ms p50 on user-facing calls.
- Top integration items we flagged: SDK setup & auth, routing (canary/model variants), structured output/tool-calling for downstream actions, embeddings + reranker flow, and observability hooks for correlation and latency breakdowns.

Observability asks you mentioned we should cover:
- Trace IDs / request IDs that we can wire into your logs
- Per-request latency breakdown headers (inbound processing, model inference, tokenization/decoding)
- Log field recommendations (model_id, model_version, route, tenant_id, prompt_bucket)
- Dashboard template (per-route latency, token cost, error traces, reranker score distribution)

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share a short tech note with header names and sample JSON for logs and structured output.
2) Vivek (cc'd) will scope a quick example for your engineers — SDK call samples + auth options.
3) Schedule a 30-min follow-up deep dive (we suggested Mon/Tue next week) to walk through the sample and answer auth/routing questions.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf (quickstart + sample calls), redwood-observability-field-spec.md (observability fields).

Open items for FinTechCo: are you leaning toward service-account API keys for server-side calls, or user-scoped tokens for any client-side flows? Also — do you have existing trace/request-id header conventions we should adopt?

Thanks — talk soon.

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few quick clarifications from our side:
- Auth: for server-side inference we'll use service accounts / API keys; for any in-browser assistant experiments we'd prefer a short-lived token flow (so if you can outline OAuth or token-exchange patterns that'd help).
- Trace headers: we already send X-Request-ID and X-B3-TraceId through our infra; if Redwood can accept those as passthrough that'd be ideal. If you have preferred header names we can map at the edge.
- Reranker: interested in an estimate for the token overhead and latency impact if we run a dense embedding + lightweight neural reranker for top-K (K=20) results. Latency budget for user searches is 150-200ms p50.

We're available Tue 17 Feb 11:00-12:00 PT or Wed 18 Feb 09:00-11:00 PT for the technical deep dive.

Appreciate the attachments — will review and come with a couple sample traces from our side.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Discovery — Redwood integration / observability items (technical details + examples)

Thanks Marissa — attaching the two brief artifacts (redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf and redwood-observability-field-spec.md). Below are the highlights / examples so Alex's team can prototype quickly: 

1) Auth patterns
- Server-to-server: API key (service account) header: Authorization: Bearer <REDWOOD_API_KEY>
- Client flows: short-lived tokens via token-exchange (we support OAuth 2.0 + minting short TTL tokens from a backend)

2) Trace / request IDs (recommended)
- Accept and preserve common headers: X-Request-ID, X-B3-TraceId, traceparent
- Recommended Redwood passthrough / canonical header: X-Redwood-Trace (value: same as upstream trace id)
- Example: X-Request-ID: 8f14e45fceea167a5a36dedd4bea2543

3) Latency breakdown headers (response)
- X-Redwood-Latency-Total: 120ms
- X-Redwood-Latency-Frontend: 8ms
- X-Redwood-Latency-Model: 95ms
- X-Redwood-Latency-PostProcess: 17ms
- We also emit per-token counters to metrics (tokens.inferred) with histogram buckets.

4) Logging / structured fields (recommended minimal set)
- log fields to include: {"timestamp", "request_id", "trace_id", "tenant_id", "route", "model_id", "model_version", "inference_ms", "tokens_out", "reranker_score"}
- Sample flattened log JSON line (one-line): {"timestamp":"2026-02-18T16:44:10Z","request_id":"8f14e45f","trace_id":"b7f3...","tenant_id":"fintechco-prod","route":"/v1/chat/completions","model_id":"redwood-v2-small","inference_ms":95,"tokens_out":42}

5) Structured output / tool-calling (example)
- We recommend a concise schema for actions: 
  {"action_type":"approve_payment","confidence":0.93,"arguments": {"payment_id":"p-12345","amount":200.00},"metadata":{"source":"assistant-v2"}}
- The SDK supports both explicit tool invocation and a structured response parse helper that validates against a JSON schema before returning to your service.

6) Embeddings + reranker guidance
- Suggest pipeline: candidate retrieval (ANN) -> embed candidates + query with Resizable embedding model -> compute scores -> rerank top-K (K=20) with a lightweight cross-encoder reranker.
- Token overhead: embedding calls are lightweight (only per-document vectorization done in batch). Reranker (cross-encoder) for K=20 typically adds ~30-60ms on optimized GPU paths; end-to-end estimate depends on candidate fetch time. We can provide a bench of your sample corpus if you share a small dataset.

7) Dashboards / templates
- Uploaded a Grafana dashboard JSON as a template in the Drive link; includes per-route p50/p95 latency, per-model token cost, reranker score distribution panels, and top error traces.

Next steps:
- Alex: drop a sample trace or a small dataset for baseline bench (we can run a quick perf estimate).
- Marissa / Stephanie: I'll prepare a 2-slide perf estimate for Wed's call and bring the quickstart code samples to demo.
